withSignature(string $signature): self
withHeader(string $name, string $value): selfEscape hatch for arbitrary headers (RFC 5322 §3.6 optional-field set): List-Unsubscribe, In-Reply-To, X-… anything the fixed message fields do not already own. Names are validated against the RFC 9110 token grammar, values ride the SAME CRLF + C0 refusal class the subject gate uses, and the pair accumulates in insertion order (a later same-name header overwrites the value but keeps its original position; the comparison is case-insensitive per RFC 5321 §2.3.1 — X- prefixed names are always open, the fixed set below is what this class and the transports compose themselves and cannot be overridden from here): From, To, Cc, Bcc (never travels as a header at all), Subject, Reply-To, Date, Message-ID, MIME-Version, Content-Type, Content-Transfer-Encoding.
bodyWithSignature(): ?stringBody text with signature appended (if set).
allRecipients(): arrayAll recipients combined (to + cc + bcc) for SMTP "RCPT TO" routing.

SmtpTransport final class

Sends email via direct SMTP (TCP/TLS).

MethodSummary
static isValidHost(string $host): boolConstruction-time input floors — one home for the bounds.
static isValidPort(int $port): bool
static isValidTimeout(int $timeout): bool
__construct(string $host, int $port = 587, string $username = '', #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password = '', int $timeout = 30, string $heloHost = '', ?bool $assumeOpenssl = null)
withRequireTls(bool $require = true): selfControl whether the send fails when the channel cannot be encrypted.
withImplicitTls(bool $implicit = true): selfReturn a copy that connects with implicit TLS (SMTPS) regardless of port.
withCaFile(string $caFile): selfReturn a copy that verifies the server certificate against a custom CA bundle instead of the system trust store (e.g. a private CA).
__debugInfo(): arrayMask secrets so the SMTP password never leaks through var_dump() or print_r() reflection of live object state.
__serialize(): arrayRefuse serialisation outright: a serialised transport is a plaintext credential on disk or in a cache, and unserialize() of it resurrected a live credentialed sender. Transports are cheap to build where they are used; there is nothing worth persisting in one.
static __set_state(array $properties): staticRefuse var_export() resurrection — see the __debugInfo contract above for what this does and does not seal.
send(Email $email, ?CancellationToken $token = null): voidSend an email with optional cancellation support.
name(): string
buildMimeMessage(Email $email, bool $allow8Bit = true): stringRender the full RFC 2046 MIME message for an email (headers + body).
